archive-restore.visual: A wide rectangular box with a thick horizontal lid across the top and squared lower corners, drawn in outline style. The lid has a narrow raised lip along its top edge. From inside the box, an upward-pointing arrow rises through the open top, indicating content being lifted out of storage.
archive-restore.usage: Unarchive or restore an item from archive, export from a storage container, retrieve a stored file, move content out of a folder.

zoom-out.visual: A circular lens with a short horizontal dash (minus sign) centered inside it, attached to a diagonal handle extending from the lower-right of the circle toward the bottom-right corner. The handle is slightly thicker than the circle's outline stroke.
zoom-out.usage: Zoom out on a map or image, decrease text size, remove a search filter, collapse a detail view.

badge-check.visual: A rounded outline shape with a continuous scalloped or pinched edge forming roughly 8–10 small inward curves around the perimeter, giving the appearance of a decorative seal or starburst badge. A bold checkmark is centered inside the badge, with the tick's left leg shorter and the right leg longer, angled upward.
badge-check.usage: Verified account or identity badge; certified or approved status on a listing; trust indicator next to a username; marking a completed certification or credential.

info.visual: A smooth, perfectly round circle outline containing a lowercase letter 'i' centered inside. The 'i' consists of a small filled dot above a short vertical stroke, both centered on the circle's vertical axis.
info.usage: Inline information tooltip trigger; informational status indicator next to a label; help text toggle; neutral informational notice in a notification system.

camera-off.visual: A camera body with a wide rounded rectangular shape, a small raised bump on the top-left edge, and a circular lens outline in the center — all rendered in outline style. A bold diagonal line runs from the lower-left corner to the upper-right corner of the composition, crossing through the entire camera shape to indicate it is disabled or unavailable.
camera-off.usage: Camera permission denied states, disabling camera in video call settings, indicating no camera detected, muting video input in a conference call.

bell-dot.visual: A bell shape drawn in outline style: a symmetrical dome that widens from a narrow top, flaring out to curved sides, with a small clapper bump centered at the bottom. A small filled circle sits at the upper-right of the bell dome, overlapping or adjacent to the outer edge, serving as a notification badge indicator.
bell-dot.usage: Unread notification indicator, new alert badge on the notification icon, unseen activity alert, push notification pending state.

lock-open.visual: A padlock body rendered as a wide rounded rectangle in outline style, with a U-shaped shackle (the arched bar that normally passes through the lock) that is open: the shackle's left leg connects to the top-left of the body while the right leg rises freely and curves away to the right, leaving the top of the lock body open.
lock-open.usage: Unlocked or public content states, disabling a lock action, unsecured connection warnings, toggling permissions off.

shield-alert.visual: A shield outline with straight sides that taper inward toward a pointed bottom tip, and a slightly curved top edge — similar to a classic heraldic shield silhouette. A bold exclamation mark is centered inside: a short vertical stroke above a small dot, indicating a warning or alert state.
shield-alert.usage: Security warning or vulnerability alert, account at risk notification, failed security check, suspicious activity banner.

shield-check.visual: A shield outline with straight sides that taper inward toward a pointed bottom tip, and a slightly curved top edge — similar to a classic heraldic shield silhouette. A bold checkmark is centered inside, with its short left leg angling down and its longer right leg sweeping up, indicating a verified or secure state.
shield-check.usage: Verified or trusted status badge, successful security scan result, secure transaction confirmation, two-factor authentication success.

shield-x.visual: A shield outline with straight sides that taper inward toward a pointed bottom tip, and a slightly curved top edge — similar to a classic heraldic shield silhouette. A bold X mark is centered inside, formed by two diagonal strokes crossing at the midpoint, indicating rejection, failure, or a blocked state.
shield-x.usage: Security check failed, blocked or rejected access, antivirus threat detected, permission denied indicator.
